summary: Phase I-4c of the immutable Nex Core plan: the Controller guest image profile (image/controller, image/build.sh controller, image/release.py controller: read-only erofs+verity system disk as a raw GPT image, UEFI only, plus the persistent controller-data.qcow2 layout at /var), appliance/build.py --profile controller emitting the vm-image component entry, deploy wiring of internal/vmhost's two-disk profile (nex-core-local --controller-system-image, core-local-setup configure --controller-image-sha256, profile seed without the update helper, UEFI with Secure Boot pinned off), forge-only image CI workflows, a QEMU boot test of the guest, and the owner-approved policy wording in AGENTS.md, PRODUCT.md and README.md. The Controller's APT helpers, routes and panel are kept for the classic edition and the single-disk appliance. Review fixes of 2026-10-02 to the guest image (not rebuilt, not booted): the nex-controller account has fixed uid and gid 280 from a sysusers.d entry, verified by the postinst, so the owner firstboot gives the data disk files cannot shift between image builds; the image installs systemd-resolved (with the resolv.conf link) and systemd-timesyncd.

guide.reason: docs/guide/deploy-controller-appliance.md now says the two-disk Controller image exists, how a host is told to deploy it, and that nothing was walked through; marked unverified (the image booted once under QEMU, Core has not deployed it).

api.reason: No HTTP, RPC, report or protocol change. The new surface is a nex-core-local command-line flag pair, a core-local-setup option and the libvirt domain XML of the already documented two-disk profile (UEFI with Secure Boot off); the Controller's own routes, including its APT update routes, are unchanged.

roadmap.reason: Phase I-4 of a plan whose options were approved on 2026-10-02 but whose phases are not accepted; development work validated in simulation only. No published milestone changed.

state.reason: The Controller guest keeps only /var/lib/nex-controller and /etc/nex-controller (the closed list recovery already enumerates) on controller-data.qcow2; the system image, the checkpoint and the swap journal belong to the Core that hosts it. The deploy option is Core host configuration. No new Controller-owned data.
state.record: /etc/nex/core-local.env key controller_image_sha256 (host configuration), the staged component /var/lib/nex/payload/<sha256>/controller-system.img, the deployment journal's system field, and in the guest the data disk's /var (ext4) with the /etc overlay upper layer at /var/lib/nex/etc. A fresh Controller recovers nothing from this slice.

verification.method: Docker builds of the guest image with appliance/build.py --profile controller and image/build.sh controller (pinned snapshot, capped containers); tests/integration/controller_image_boot.py under QEMU/KVM with OVMF (first boot, reboot on the same data disk, one-byte tamper); go test -p 1 ./internal/vmhost ./cmd/nex-core-local; python3 -m unittest tests.test_core_local_package tests.test_appliance_build tests.test_image_layout tests.test_ci_security; scripts/check_docs.py --worktree; the repository privacy test. Simulation only: no libvirt, Core deployment, swap, pool or browser. Review fixes (account ids, resolver, time sync): python3 -m unittest tests.test_image_composition (the account entry through the real systemd-sysusers --root on a scratch tree); package contents read from the pinned snapshot. The guest image was not rebuilt or booted after these fixes.
